title: What Databricks is
md:
Databricks is a managed data and AI platform built around Apache Spark and Delta Lake. It runs on Azure, AWS and GCP. You get managed Spark clusters, a SQL engine, notebooks, orchestration, governance (Unity Catalog) and ML tools in one workspace, reading and writing data in your own cloud storage.

#### The lakehouse idea

|  | Data Data lake warehouse | Lakehouse |
|---|---|---|
| Storage | Cheap object storage, open Proprietary files storage | Cheap object storage, open table formats |
| Data types | Any (structured, semi, Structured unstructured) | Any |
| ACID transactions | No Yes | Yes (Delta / Iceberg) |
| Performance for BI | Poor without extra work Excellent | Good to excellent |
| Workloads | Data science, raw storage BI, reporting | Both on one copy of data |

The lakehouse keeps data in open formats on cloud storage, adds a transaction layer (Delta Lake) for reliability, and adds governance and fast engines on top.

#### Control plane and compute plane

- **Control plane** (managed by Databricks): the web app, notebooks, job scheduler, cluster manager, Unity Catalog metadata.
- **Compute plane:** where clusters actually run and process data.
- Classic compute runs in **your** cloud account (VNet/VPC).
- Serverless compute runs in Databricks' account, starts in seconds, and is managed for you.
- **Data** stays in your cloud storage (ADLS Gen2, S3, GCS).

#### Account and workspaces

- An **account** holds users, groups, Unity Catalog metastores and billing.
- A **workspace** is an environment where teams build: notebooks, jobs, clusters. Companies usually have workspaces per environment (dev / test / prod) or per business unit, all attached to the same Unity Catalog metastore for a region.

title: Workspace objects
md:
| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| Notebook | Interactive document with cells in Python, SQL, Scala or R |
| Git folder (Repos) | A Git repository cloned into the workspace — the way to version code |
| Workspace files | Python modules, configs and other files stored in the workspace |
| Catalog Explorer | UI to browse catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, lineage and permissions |
| Jobs | Scheduled/triggered workflows (Lakeflow Jobs) |
| Pipelines | Declarative ETL pipelines (Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, formerly Delta Live Tables) |
| SQL editor, queries, dashboards, alerts | Databricks SQL objects |
| Compute | Clusters, SQL warehouses, pools |

#### Development flow

1. Develop in notebooks or Python files inside a Git folder.

2. Commit and push to a branch; raise a pull request.

3. CI runs tests and deploys to test, then prod, using Databricks Asset Bundles or the CLI/API.

4. Production runs as jobs, not as manually executed notebooks.

title: Compute
md:
#### Types of compute

| Compute | Purpose | Billing pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **All-purpose cluster** | Interactive development, shared by users | More expensive per DBU |
| **Job cluster** | Created for one job run, terminated after | Cheaper per DBU; isolated per run |
| **Serverless compute (notebooks,** **jobs, pipelines)** | Instant start, no cluster management | Pay per use; managed by Databricks |
| **SQL warehouse** (classic / pro / serverless) | SQL queries, BI tools, dashboards | Per warehouse uptime |
| **Instance pool** | Keeps idle VMs ready to cut cluster start time | VM cost while idle |

> Production pipelines should run on **job clusters or serverless jobs**, not on all-purpose clusters. They're cheaper, isolated, and start clean every run.

#### Cluster configuration choices

- **Databricks Runtime (DBR):** a bundle of Spark version, Delta, libraries and optimizations. Use an **LTS** (long-term support) version in production. ML runtimes add ML libraries.
- **Photon:** Databricks' vectorized C++ engine for SQL and DataFrame operations. Big speedups for scans, joins, aggregations; higher DBU rate. Not used for Python UDFs or RDD code.
- **Node types:** memory-optimized for joins/caching, compute-optimized for CPU-heavy work, storage-optimized (local SSD) for disk cache and heavy shuffles.
- **Autoscaling:** min and max workers; Databricks adds workers when tasks queue up.
- **Auto-termination:** stop idle all-purpose clusters after N minutes.
- **Spot instances:** cheaper VMs that the cloud can reclaim — good for workers on fault-tolerant batch jobs; keep the driver on-demand.
- **Single-node clusters:** driver only — for small data, pandas, testing.

#### Access modes (Unity Catalog)

| Mode | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Standard (formerly shared) | Multiple users, isolated from each other | Recommended default; some low-level APIs restricted |
| Dedicated (formerly single user) | One user or group | Full API support (RDD, some ML libraries) |
| No isolation (legacy) | Anyone | No Unity Catalog — avoid |

#### Cluster policies

Admins define policies that limit what users can create: allowed node types, max workers, mandatory tags, required auto-termination. Policies are the main way to control cost and enforce standards.

#### Libraries and init scripts

- Install Python wheels, PyPI packages or Maven JARs at cluster, notebook (`%pip install`) or job-task level.
- Init scripts run on each node at startup (install OS packages, set environment). Store them in workspace files or volumes.
- Prefer pinned versions and a private package index for reproducibility.

title: Notebooks and dbutils
md:
#### Magic commands

```text
%python  %sql  %scala  %r     switch language for a cell
%md                           markdown documentation
%sh                           shell command on the driver
%fs ls /Volumes/main/raw/landing        file system commands
%pip install pkg==1.2.3       notebook-scoped Python library
%run ./utils/common           run another notebook inline (shares variables)
```

#### dbutils

```text
dbutils.fs.ls("/Volumes/main/raw/landing/")
dbutils.fs.cp(src, dst, recurse=True)
dbutils.fs.rm(path, recurse=True)
dbutils.fs.mkdirs(path)
dbutils.secrets.get(scope="kv-prod", key="sql-password")     # value is redacted in output
dbutils.secrets.listScopes()
dbutils.widgets.text("run_date", "2026-01-15")
run_date = dbutils.widgets.get("run_date")
result = dbutils.notebook.run("./child", timeout_seconds=600, arguments={"run_date": run_date})
dbutils.notebook.exit("ok")                                  # return a value to the caller
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="row_count", value=12345)    # pass values between job tasks
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.get(taskKey="extract", key="row_count", default=0)
```

#### %run vs dbutils.notebook.run

|  | `%run` | `dbutils.notebook.run` |
|---|---|---|
| Runs in | Same context | Separate ephemeral job |
| Shares variables/functions | Yes | No — only string arguments in, one string out |
| Use for | Including shared helper code | Orchestrating notebooks with parameters, parallel runs |

For production, prefer Python modules (imported normally) and job tasks over notebook chaining.

#### display

`display(df)` renders a table with built-in charts and profiling. It runs a limited query (first rows), so it doesn't show totals — use explicit aggregations to check counts.

title: Storage and data access
md:
#### Paths you'll see

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `abfss://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/path` ADLS Gen2 (Azure) |  |
| `s3://bucket/path` | Amazon S3 |
| `gs://bucket/path` | Google Cloud Storage |
| `/Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/path` | Unity Catalog volume (governed files) |
| `dbfs:/...` | Databricks File System — legacy workspace storage |
| `/mnt/...` | DBFS mounts — legacy, replaced by external locations and volumes |

#### Unity Catalog way of accessing storage

1. **Storage credential:** wraps cloud identity — on Azure, an Azure Databricks access connector (managed identity) with RBAC on the storage account.

2. **External location:** a storage path + a storage credential. Grant `READ FILES` / `WRITE` `FILES` / `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` on it.

3. **Volumes:** governed folders for non-tabular files (CSV drops, images, JARs). Managed or external.

4. **Tables:** managed or external, governed by Unity Catalog.

```sql norun
CREATE STORAGE CREDENTIAL IF NOT EXISTS lake_cred ...;      -- usually created by admins in
UI/Terraform
CREATE EXTERNAL LOCATION raw_landing
  URL 'abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/landing'
  WITH (STORAGE CREDENTIAL lake_cred);
GRANT READ FILES ON EXTERNAL LOCATION raw_landing TO `data-engineers`;
CREATE VOLUME main.raw.landing;                              -- managed volume
```

> Avoid mounts and account keys in notebooks. With Unity Catalog, access is granted to identities, audited, and nobody handles storage keys.

title: Unity Catalog
md:
Unity Catalog (UC) is Databricks' governance layer: one place to manage data objects, permissions, lineage and auditing across workspaces.

#### Object hierarchy

```text
Metastore (one per region, attached to workspaces)
└── Catalog            e.g. dev, prod, or by domain: sales, finance
    └── Schema         (database) e.g. bronze, silver, gold
        ├── Table      managed or external
        ├── View / materialized view
        ├── Volume     files
        ├── Function   SQL/Python UDFs
        └── Model      ML models
```

Three-level names everywhere: `catalog.schema.table` — for example `prod.silver.orders`.

#### Managed vs external tables

|  | Managed | External |
|---|---|---|
| Data location | UC-managed storage location | A path you specify (in an external location) |
| `DROP TABLE` | Deletes data (recoverable for a short period) | Leaves the files |
| Maintenance | Eligible for predictive optimization | You run OPTIMIZE/VACUUM yourself |
| Recommended Default for new tables |  | When other tools must own the files or paths are fixed |

#### Permissions

```sql norun
GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG prod TO `analysts`;
GRANT USE SCHEMA ON SCHEMA prod.gold TO `analysts`;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE prod.gold.daily_sales TO `analysts`;
GRANT MODIFY ON SCHEMA prod.silver TO `etl-service-principal`;
GRANT CREATE TABLE ON SCHEMA dev.sandbox TO `data-engineers`;
REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE prod.gold.customers FROM `contractors`;
SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE prod.gold.daily_sales;
```

- Privileges are inherited downward: `SELECT` on a schema applies to all its tables.
- To read a table you need `USE CATALOG` + `USE SCHEMA` + `SELECT`.
- Grant to **groups**, not individuals. Run production jobs as **service principals**.
- Every object has an **owner** who can grant on it.

#### Fine-grained security

```sql norun
-- row filter: users see only their region
CREATE FUNCTION prod.sec.region_filter(region STRING)
RETURN is_account_group_member('admins') OR region = current_user_region();   -- illustrative
logic
ALTER TABLE prod.gold.sales SET ROW FILTER prod.sec.region_filter ON (region);
-- column mask: hide email except for a group
CREATE FUNCTION prod.sec.mask_email(email STRING)
RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('pii-readers') THEN email ELSE '***' END;
ALTER TABLE prod.silver.customers ALTER COLUMN email SET MASK prod.sec.mask_email;
```

Dynamic views (views using `current_user()` / `is_account_group_member()`) are the older way to do the same.

#### Lineage, audit and discovery

- **Lineage:** UC captures table- and column-level lineage automatically for queries run on UC-enabled compute — which jobs and notebooks read and write each table.
- **Audit logs:** who accessed what, available in system tables.
- **Tags and comments:** classify sensitive columns (`pii`), document tables for discovery.
- **System tables** (`system.*`): billing usage, audit, lineage, job runs, query history — query them with SQL for cost and operations reporting.

#### Delta Sharing

Open protocol to share live tables with other organizations or platforms without copying data. Recipients can read from Databricks, Spark, pandas or BI tools.

title: Delta Lake
md:
Delta Lake is the default table format on Databricks: Parquet files plus a **transaction log** (`_delta_log/`) that records every change.

#### How the transaction log works

```text
/prod/silver/orders/
├── _delta_log/
│   ├── 00000000000000000000.json     version 0: add files A, B
│   ├── 00000000000000000001.json     version 1: add file C
│   ├── 00000000000000000002.json     version 2: remove B, add D  (an UPDATE)
│   └── 00000000000000000010.checkpoint.parquet   periodic snapshot of the log
├── part-000A.snappy.parquet
├── part-000C.snappy.parquet
└── part-000D.snappy.parquet
```

- Each commit is a new JSON file listing files **added** and **removed**, plus metadata and stats (min/max per column for data skipping).
- Readers compute the current table from the log, so they never see half-written results — **atomic commits**.
- Concurrent writers use **optimistic concurrency**: if two commits touch the same files, one fails with a conflict and can retry.
- Updates and deletes don't modify files in place; they write new files and mark old ones removed (or use deletion vectors).

#### ACID on a data lake

| Property | How Delta gives it |
|---|---|
| Atomicity | A commit file is written or not; partial writes are invisible |
| Consistency | Schema enforcement, constraints |
| Isolation | Snapshot isolation for reads; write conflict detection |
| Durability | Data and log on durable cloud storage |

#### Creating and writing

```python norun
CREATE TABLE prod.silver.orders (
  order_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  customer_id BIGINT,
  amount DECIMAL(18,2),
  order_ts TIMESTAMP,
  order_date DATE GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CAST(order_ts AS DATE)),
  CONSTRAINT positive_amount CHECK (amount >= 0)
)
CLUSTER BY (order_date, customer_id)
COMMENT 'Cleaned orders, one row per order';
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("prod.silver.orders")
(df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite")
   .option("replaceWhere", "order_date = '2026-01-15'")
   .saveAsTable("prod.silver.orders"))
```

#### Schema enforcement and evolution

- **Enforcement:** writes with mismatched columns or types fail — bad data can't silently corrupt the table.
- **Evolution:** allow new columns explicitly.

```python norun
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").option("mergeSchema", "true").saveAsTable("t")
spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled", "true")   # for MERGE
ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMNS (channel STRING);
ALTER TABLE t SET TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.columnMapping.mode' = 'name');  -- enables
rename/drop column
ALTER TABLE t RENAME COLUMN status TO order_status;
```

#### DML

```sql norun
UPDATE prod.silver.orders SET status = 'CANCELLED' WHERE order_id = 1001;
DELETE FROM prod.silver.orders WHERE order_date < '2020-01-01';
MERGE INTO prod.silver.customers t
USING updates s ON t.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'D' THEN DELETE
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND s.op <> 'D' THEN INSERT *
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE AND t.is_active THEN UPDATE SET is_active = false;
```

`WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE` handles target rows missing from the source — useful for full-snapshot syncs.

#### Time travel and restore

```sql norun
DESCRIBE HISTORY prod.silver.orders;                         -- versions, operations, who, when
SELECT * FROM prod.silver.orders VERSION AS OF 42;
SELECT * FROM prod.silver.orders TIMESTAMP AS OF '2026-01-15 06:00:00';
RESTORE TABLE prod.silver.orders TO VERSION AS OF 42;         -- undo a bad load
```

Time travel works only while old files still exist — `VACUUM` removes them after the retention period.

#### OPTIMIZE, Z-order and liquid clustering

```sql norun
OPTIMIZE prod.silver.orders;                                  -- compact small files
OPTIMIZE prod.silver.orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-01-01'; -- partitioned tables: limit scope
OPTIMIZE prod.silver.orders ZORDER BY (customer_id);          -- co-locate values (legacy
approach)
```

**Liquid clustering** is the current recommended layout for new tables. It replaces partitioning + Z-order for most cases.

```sql norun
CREATE TABLE t (...) CLUSTER BY (customer_id, order_date);
ALTER TABLE t CLUSTER BY (region);                -- keys can change without rewriting all
data
ALTER TABLE t CLUSTER BY AUTO;                    -- let Databricks pick keys from query
patterns
OPTIMIZE t;                                       -- clusters incrementally
```

|  | Hive-style partitioning | Z-order | Liquid clustering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layout | Folders per value | Re-sorts files on OPTIMIZE | Incremental clustering |
| Change keys | Rewrite table | Rerun on all data | `ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY` |
| Small tables / high cardinality | Bad (tiny files) | OK | Good |
| Recommended for new tables | Only for very large tables with clear date filters | Legacy | Yes |

#### VACUUM and retention

```sql norun
VACUUM prod.silver.orders;                    -- remove unreferenced files older than retention
(default 7 days)
VACUUM prod.silver.orders RETAIN 168 HOURS;
ALTER TABLE t SET TBLPROPERTIES (
  'delta.deletedFileRetentionDuration' = '30 days',
  'delta.logRetentionDuration' = '60 days');
```

Shorter retention saves storage but limits time travel and can break long-running readers or streams that still need old files.

#### Deletion vectors

With deletion vectors enabled, `DELETE`, `UPDATE` and `MERGE` mark removed rows in a small side file instead of rewriting whole Parquet files. Writes are much faster; files are physically rewritten later by `OPTIMIZE`/purge.

#### Change Data Feed (CDF)

```python norun
ALTER TABLE prod.silver.orders SET TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true);
SELECT * FROM table_changes('prod.silver.orders', 120);      -- changes since version 120
changes = (spark.read.format("delta").option("readChangeFeed", "true")
           .option("startingVersion", 120).table("prod.silver.orders"))
# _change_type: insert, update_preimage, update_postimage, delete
```

CDF lets downstream tables process only what changed instead of rescanning everything.

#### Cloning

```sql norun
CREATE TABLE dev.silver.orders_copy SHALLOW CLONE prod.silver.orders;   -- metadata only,
points to same files
CREATE TABLE backup.silver.orders_2026_01 DEEP CLONE prod.silver.orders; -- full independent
copy
```

Shallow clones are perfect for testing a change on production-sized data without copying it.

#### Other useful features

- **Identity columns:** `id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` for surrogate keys.
- **Generated columns:** derive `order_date` from `order_ts` automatically.
- **Constraints:** `NOT NULL`, `CHECK` (enforced); primary/foreign keys (informational).
- **UniForm:** writes Iceberg (and Hudi) metadata alongside Delta so Iceberg readers can read the same table.
- **Table properties:** `delta.autoOptimize.optimizeWrite`, `delta.autoOptimize.autoCompact`, `delta.appendOnly`, `delta.enableDeletionVectors`.

title: Medallion architecture
md:
#### The three layers

| Layer | Content | Typical operations | Tables |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bronze** Raw data as ingested, append- | only, plus metadata (`_ingest_ts`, `_source_file`) | Auto Loader / streaming append | Streaming tables, wide strings or raw JSON |
| **Silver** | Cleaned, typed, deduplicated, conformed entities | Parsing, casting, dedup, MERGE, SCD, quality checks | One table per business entity |
| **Gold** | Business-ready: facts, dimensions, aggregates, features | Joins, aggregations, KPIs | Star schemas, reporting tables, materialized views |

#### Design principles

- Bronze keeps raw history so you can **reprocess** when logic changes or bugs are found.
- Silver is the **single source of truth** for each entity; downstream teams build on it.
- Gold is shaped for specific consumers (BI, ML, APIs) and can be rebuilt from silver.
- Each layer is idempotent and incremental where possible.
- Map layers to Unity Catalog: `prod.bronze.*`, `prod.silver.*`, `prod.gold.*` (or catalogs per layer/domain).

title: Ingestion
md:
#### Auto Loader

Auto Loader incrementally ingests new files from cloud storage as they arrive, tracking which files were processed in the stream checkpoint.

```python norun
(spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
   .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
   .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", "/Volumes/prod/meta/schemas/orders")
   .option("cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes", "true")
   .option("cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode", "addNewColumns")
   .load("abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/")
   .selectExpr("*", "_metadata.file_path AS _source_file", "current_timestamp() AS _ingest_ts")
 .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/Volumes/prod/meta/checkpoints/orders_bronze")
   .option("mergeSchema", "true")
   .trigger(availableNow=True)
   .toTable("prod.bronze.orders"))
```

Key features:

- **Schema inference and evolution:** schema stored at `schemaLocation`; new columns handled by `schemaEvolutionMode` (`addNewColumns`, `rescue`, `failOnNewColumns`, `none`).
- **Rescued data column (**`_rescued_data`**):** values that don't fit the schema are kept here instead of being lost.
- **File discovery:** directory listing (default, simple) or file notification mode (cloud events + queue — scales to millions of files).
- `trigger(availableNow=True)`**:** run as a scheduled batch job that processes only new files, then stops.

#### COPY INTO

```text
COPY INTO prod.bronze.orders
FROM 'abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/'
FILEFORMAT = CSV
FORMAT_OPTIONS ('header' = 'true')
COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema' = 'true');
```

Idempotent SQL load: files already loaded are skipped. Good for simpler, lower-volume batch loads; Auto Loader scales better.

#### Lakeflow Connect

Managed connectors that ingest from SaaS applications and databases (for example Salesforce, SQL Server, and others) into Unity Catalog tables with minimal code, including incremental/CDC ingestion for supported sources.

#### Other sources

- **Kafka / Azure Event Hubs:** Structured Streaming with the Kafka source (Event Hubs exposes a Kafka endpoint).
- **JDBC databases:** `spark.read.format("jdbc")` with parallel partitioning, or Lakeflow Connect, or ADF copying into the lake first.
- **Lakehouse Federation:** query external databases (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, etc.) through Unity Catalog without copying data — good for exploration and small lookups, not heavy ETL.

title: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (formerly Delta Live Tables)
md:
Declarative pipelines let you define **what** tables should contain; Databricks works out the dependency graph, runs it incrementally, manages checkpoints, retries, and enforces data-quality rules. The engine is now open-sourced as Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines.

#### Dataset types

| Type | Behaviour | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| **Streaming** **table** | Processes each input row once, incrementally (append) | Bronze ingestion, append-only silver, CDC targets |
| **Materialized** **view** | Result kept up to date; recomputed incrementally where possible | Silver/gold transformations with joins and aggregations |
| **View** (temporary) | Not stored; intermediate logic inside the pipeline | Reusable steps |

#### SQL example

```sql norun
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE bronze_orders
AS SELECT *, _metadata.file_path AS source_file
FROM STREAM read_files('abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/', format => 'json');
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE silver_orders (
  CONSTRAINT valid_id     EXPECT (order_id IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW,
  CONSTRAINT valid_amount EXPECT (amount >= 0)          ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE,
  CONSTRAINT has_email    EXPECT (email IS NOT NULL)
)
AS SELECT CAST(order_id AS BIGINT) order_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(18,2)) amount,
lower(email) email, order_ts
FROM STREAM(bronze_orders);
CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW gold_daily_sales
AS SELECT DATE(order_ts) order_date, SUM(amount) revenue, COUNT(*) orders
FROM silver_orders GROUP BY DATE(order_ts);
```

#### Python example

```python norun
from pyspark import pipelines as dp      # older pipelines: import dlt  (@dlt.table, @dlt.expect)
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
@dp.table(comment="Raw orders from landing")
def bronze_orders():
    return (spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
            .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
            .load("abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/"))
@dp.table
@dp.expect_or_drop("valid_id", "order_id IS NOT NULL")
def silver_orders():
    return spark.readStream.table("bronze_orders").withColumn("amount",
F.col("amount").cast("decimal(18,2)"))
```

#### Expectations (data quality)

| Clause | On violation |
|---|---|
| `EXPECT (...)` | Keep the row, record the metric |
| `... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW` | Drop the row, record it |
| `... ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE` | Stop the update |

Expectation metrics appear in the pipeline UI and event log, so quality is measured continuously.

#### CDC and SCD with AUTO CDC (APPLY CHANGES)

```sql norun
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE dim_customer;
APPLY CHANGES INTO dim_customer          -- newer syntax: CREATE FLOW ... AS AUTO CDC
INTO ...
FROM STREAM(bronze_customer_cdc)
KEYS (customer_id)
APPLY AS DELETE WHEN op = 'D'
SEQUENCE BY op_ts                        -- orders out-of-order events correctly
COLUMNS * EXCEPT (op, op_ts)
STORED AS SCD TYPE 2;                    -- or SCD TYPE 1
```

This replaces a lot of hand-written MERGE logic: ordering by sequence column, deletes, and SCD2 history columns (`__START_AT`, `__END_AT`) are handled for you.

#### Running pipelines

- **Triggered** (process available data, then stop — scheduled by a job) or **continuous** (always on, low latency).
- **Development mode:** reuses the cluster, no automatic retries — fast iteration. **Production mode:** retries on failure, restarts clusters.
- Full refresh rebuilds tables from scratch; normal updates are incremental.
- The **event log** records lineage, data-quality metrics, progress and errors — queryable as a table.

title: Lakeflow Jobs (orchestration)
md:
#### Building blocks

| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Job | A workflow with one or more tasks |
| Task | One unit: notebook, Python script, Python wheel, SQL file/query, dbt, pipeline, JAR, another job, If/else, For each |
| Dependencies Tasks form a DAG; a task runs when its upstream tasks succeed (configurable: | all succeeded, at least one, all done, etc.) |
| Compute | Job cluster (per job or shared across tasks), serverless, or SQL warehouse for SQL tasks |
| Parameters | Job parameters passed to every task; dynamic values like `{{job.start_time.iso_date}}` |
| Task values | Small values passed between tasks (`dbutils.jobs.taskValues`) |

#### Triggers

- **Scheduled:** cron-like schedule with time zone.
- **File arrival:** run when new files land in a storage location or volume.
- **Table update:** run when upstream tables change.
- **Continuous:** restart immediately after each run (streaming jobs).
- **Manual / API:** from CI/CD, ADF or Airflow (`runs/submit`, `run-now`).

#### Reliability features

- **Retries** per task with delay; timeouts; max concurrent runs.
- **Repair run:** rerun only the failed tasks and their downstream tasks, not the whole job.
- **Notifications:** email, Slack/Teams webhooks, PagerDuty on start, success, failure, or duration threshold.
- **Run as** a service principal so production doesn't depend on a person's account.

#### A typical daily job

```text
ingest_bronze (Auto Loader, availableNow)
        │
silver_orders ── silver_customers        (parallel)
        └──────┬──────┘
         gold_daily_sales
               │
        dq_checks ──► (if/else) notify / publish
```

#### Orchestrating from outside

ADF has a native Databricks activity (notebook, Python, JAR, or run a job); Airflow has a Databricks provider (`DatabricksRunNowOperator`, `DatabricksSubmitRunOperator`). Use these when the wider workflow spans other systems; keep Databricks-internal steps inside a Databricks job.

title: Databricks SQL
md:
#### SQL warehouses

| Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| Serverless | Starts in seconds, auto-scales, managed — the usual recommendation |
| Pro | Classic compute in your account with advanced features |
| Classic | Basic, in your account |

Warehouses use Photon and are built for concurrency: many BI users and dashboards at once. Size (T-shirt sizes) controls per-query power; scaling (min/max clusters) controls concurrency.

#### What you build with it

- **SQL editor and queries** — parameterized, saved, scheduled.
- **Dashboards (AI/BI dashboards)** — visualizations over queries.
- **Alerts** — run a query on a schedule and notify when a condition is met (a freshness or data-quality alert, for example).
- **Connections from BI tools** — Power BI, Tableau, Looker via JDBC/ODBC or partner connectors.

#### Query profile

The query profile shows each operator's time, rows and bytes, spill, and whether Photon ran it — the SQL equivalent of the Spark UI. Use it to find scans that didn't prune, exploding joins and skew.

title: Performance on Databricks
md:
#### Engine-level features

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| Photon | Vectorized native execution for SQL/DataFrame operators |
| Adaptive Query Execution | Runtime join switching, partition coalescing, skew handling |
| Disk cache | Caches remote Parquet/Delta data on local SSDs of workers automatically |
| Data skipping | Min/max stats in the Delta log skip files that can't match a filter |
| Dynamic file pruning | Uses join results to skip files at runtime |
| Predictive optimization | Automatically runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE on UC managed tables |

#### File layout

- Avoid many small files: enable optimized writes and auto-compaction, or rely on predictive optimization.
- Use liquid clustering on columns used in filters and joins.
- Don't over-partition: only partition very large tables (well above 1 TB) by a low-cardinality date column, if at all.
- Keep statistics fresh (`ANALYZE TABLE ... COMPUTE STATISTICS`) when not using predictive optimization.

#### Spark-level habits (still apply)

- Broadcast small dimensions; fix skew; prune columns and filter early.
- Avoid Python UDFs; use built-in functions or pandas UDFs.
- Right-size shuffle partitions (or let AQE handle it with `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=auto` on Databricks).

#### Choosing cluster size

- Start small and scale based on the Spark UI: if CPU is saturated and tasks queue, add workers; if there's heavy spill, choose memory-optimized nodes or more partitions.
- Jobs with big shuffles benefit from storage-optimized nodes (fast local SSD).
- For many small jobs, use serverless or a pool to cut startup time.

title: Security
md:
#### Identities

- **Users** and **groups** synced from Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) via SCIM.
- **Service principals** for automation — jobs, CI/CD, external tools. Use OAuth (machine-to-machine) instead of personal access tokens where possible.
- Workspace roles (admin, user) and entitlements (cluster creation, SQL access).

#### Secrets

```bash
databricks secrets create-scope kv-prod --scope-backend-type AZURE_KEYVAULT \
  --resource-id <key-vault-resource-id> --dns-name https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/
```

- **Azure Key Vault-backed scopes:** secrets live in Key Vault; Databricks reads them.
- **Databricks-backed scopes:** stored by Databricks.
- Grant `READ` on scopes to groups/service principals. Values are redacted if printed in notebooks — but never try to print them.

#### Network security (Azure)

- **VNet injection:** deploy classic compute into your own VNet with your NSG rules and routing.
- **Secure cluster connectivity (no public IP):** cluster nodes have no public IPs.
- **Private Link:** private connectivity for users and compute to the control plane, and to storage.
- **IP access lists** for workspace access.

#### Data protection

- Unity Catalog permissions, row filters and column masks.
- Encryption at rest (cloud-managed or customer-managed keys) and in transit.
- Audit logs in system tables.

title: CI/CD and DevOps
md:
#### Git folders

Clone repos into the workspace, branch, commit and pull directly from the UI. Production should run code from a specific branch/tag deployed by CI, not from someone's personal folder.

#### Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs)

Bundles define jobs, pipelines, clusters and other resources as YAML alongside your code, and deploy them per environment.

```bash
# databricks.yml
bundle:
  name: orders_pipeline
targets:
  dev:
    mode: development
    workspace: { host: https://adb-111.azuredatabricks.net }
  prod:
    mode: production
    workspace: { host: https://adb-222.azuredatabricks.net }
    run_as: { service_principal_name: "etl-sp" }
resources:
  jobs:
    orders_daily:
      name: orders_daily
      schedule: { quartz_cron_expression: "0 0 2 * * ?", timezone_id: "Asia/Kolkata" }
      tasks:
        - task_key: ingest
          notebook_task: { notebook_path: ./src/ingest.py }
        - task_key: transform
          depends_on: [{ task_key: ingest }]
          python_wheel_task: { package_name: orders_pipeline, entry_point: main }
databricks bundle validate
databricks bundle deploy -t dev
databricks bundle run orders_daily -t dev
databricks bundle deploy -t prod          # from CI after tests pass
```

#### Typical pipeline

1. Developer works in a feature branch, deploys to dev with `bundle deploy -t dev`.

2. Pull request triggers CI: lint, unit tests (local Spark), `bundle validate`.

3. Merge to main deploys to test; integration tests run against test data.

4. Approved release deploys to prod with a service principal.

Tools: Azure DevOps Pipelines or GitHub Actions running the Databricks CLI; Terraform for workspaces, Unity Catalog objects, clusters and permissions.

#### Testing on Databricks

- Unit-test transformation functions with a local SparkSession (pytest) — fast and cheap.
- Integration tests on a small dataset in a test catalog.
- Data-quality expectations in pipelines; shallow clones of prod tables for realistic tests.

title: Cost management
md:
#### How billing works

You pay **DBUs** (Databricks Units, per second of compute, rate depends on compute type and tier) plus the **cloud VM and storage cost** for classic compute. Serverless includes the infrastructure in its DBU price.

#### Cost levers

| Lever | Effect |
|---|---|
| Job compute instead of all- purpose | Lower DBU rate for scheduled work |
| Auto-termination | Stops paying for idle clusters |
| Autoscaling with sensible max | Avoids over-provisioning |
| Spot workers | Cheaper VMs for fault-tolerant jobs |
| Serverless | No idle time, no start-up waste for short jobs |
| Photon | Higher rate but often fewer total DBUs for SQL-heavy work — measure |
| Right-sized SQL warehouses + auto-stop | BI cost control |
| Cluster policies + tags | Enforce limits, attribute cost to teams |
| Efficient code and layout | Fewer DBUs: less data scanned and shuffled |

#### Monitoring spend

```sql norun
SELECT usage_date, sku_name, SUM(usage_quantity) AS dbus
FROM system.billing.usage
WHERE usage_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 30 DAYS
GROUP BY usage_date, sku_name
ORDER BY usage_date;
```

Join billing usage with job metadata and tags to see cost per job, per team, per environment.

title: Monitoring and troubleshooting
md:
#### Where to look

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| Job run page | Task status, durations, error messages, repair runs |
| Spark UI | Stages, tasks, skew, spill, plans |
| Driver logs (stdout/stderr/log4j) | Python exceptions, stack traces |
| Cluster event log | Start, resize, termination, spot loss |
| Pipeline event log | Declarative pipeline progress, expectations, lineage |
| Query profile / query history | SQL warehouse performance |
| System tables | Job runs, billing, audit, lineage across the account |

#### Common problems

| Problem | Typical cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ConcurrentAppendException` / conflict errors | Two writes touched the same files (e.g. MERGE + OPTIMIZE, or parallel MERGEs) | Make conditions partition-specific, serialize writers, retry |
| MERGE fails: multiple source rows matched | Duplicate keys in source | Deduplicate the source first |
| Job much slower than usual | Data growth, skew, small files, cluster change | Compare runs in Spark UI, OPTIMIZE, fix skew |
| Driver OOM | `collect`/`toPandas` on large data, big broadcast | Write instead of collect, avoid broadcasting large tables |
| Stream restarted from the beginning | Checkpoint deleted or changed | Keep checkpoints stable, one per stream |
| `FileNotFoundException` reading Delta | Files vacuumed while a long reader needed them | Increase retention, avoid VACUUM with short retention |
| Permission denied | Missing UC grant (`USE CATALOG`/`USE SCHEMA`/`SELECT`) or external location access | Check `SHOW GRANTS`, grant to the right group/SP |
| Schema mismatch on write | New/changed columns | Fix upstream, or allow `mergeSchema` deliberately |

title: End-to-end example
md:
A daily orders pipeline on Azure Databricks with Unity Catalog.

#### 1. Bronze: Auto Loader ingestion

```python norun
(spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
   .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
   .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", "/Volumes/prod/meta/schemas/orders")
   .load("abfss://raw@mylake.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/")
   .select("*", F.col("_metadata.file_path").alias("_source_file"),
F.current_timestamp().alias("_ingest_ts"))
 .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/Volumes/prod/meta/checkpoints/orders_bronze")
   .trigger(availableNow=True)
   .toTable("prod.bronze.orders"))
```

#### 2. Silver: clean, dedup, MERGE

```python norun
from delta.tables import DeltaTable
from pyspark.sql import functions as F, Window as W
def upsert_silver(batch_df, batch_id):
    clean = (batch_df
      .withColumn("order_id", F.col("order_id").cast("bigint"))
      .withColumn("amount", F.col("amount").cast("decimal(18,2)"))
      .withColumn("order_ts", F.to_timestamp("order_ts"))
      .filter("order_id IS NOT NULL")
      .withColumn("rn",
F.row_number().over(W.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy(F.desc("updated_at"))))
      .filter("rn = 1").drop("rn"))
    (DeltaTable.forName(spark, "prod.silver.orders").alias("t")
       .merge(clean.alias("s"), "t.order_id = s.order_id")
       .whenMatchedUpdateAll(condition="s.updated_at > t.updated_at")
       .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
       .execute())
(spark.readStream.table("prod.bronze.orders")
   .writeStream.foreachBatch(upsert_silver)
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/Volumes/prod/meta/checkpoints/orders_silver")
   .trigger(availableNow=True)
   .start())
```

#### 3. Gold: business table

```sql norun
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE prod.gold.daily_sales
CLUSTER BY (order_date)
AS SELECT CAST(order_ts AS DATE) AS order_date, c.region,
          COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(o.amount) AS revenue
FROM prod.silver.orders o
JOIN prod.silver.customers c USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY ALL;
```

#### 4. Quality gate

```sql norun
SELECT COUNT(*) AS dupes FROM (
  SELECT order_id FROM prod.silver.orders GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);
-- task fails (or alerts) if dupes > 0
```

#### 5. Orchestrate

One Lakeflow Job: `bronze → silver → gold → dq_check`, job compute or serverless, scheduled at 02:00 IST, retries on each task, failure notification to the on-call channel, running as a service principal, deployed with an asset bundle.

> On Databricks the platform does a lot for you — but the fundamentals stay the same: idempotent writes, incremental processing, good file layout, clear ownership of each layer, and permissions granted to groups and service principals.

**— Sagar**
